Update a model's category-representation template from observations

Source: R/S7-generics.R, R/S7-update-model.R
update_template.Rd

Currently implemented for NIW_IdealAdaptor; methods for other model types will be added as their update workflows are migrated to S7.

update_template() updates the category template representations of an ideal adaptor model (NIW_IdealAdaptor, NIX_IdealAdaptor, or MNIX_IdealAdaptor) given new observations.

Usage

update_template(
  x,
  observations,
  updating = c("batch", "incremental"),
  keep_history = FALSE,
  lapse_treatment = "no_lapses",
  noise_treatment = "no_noise",
  update_method = "label-certain",
  ...
)

## S7 method for classes <MVBeliefUpdatr::NIW_IdealAdaptor>, <any>
update_template(
  x,
  observations,
  updating = c("batch", "incremental"),
  keep_history = FALSE,
  lapse_treatment = "no_lapses",
  noise_treatment = "no_noise",
  update_method = "label-certain",
  ...
)

## S7 method for classes <MVBeliefUpdatr::NIX_IdealAdaptor>, <any>
update_template(
  x,
  observations,
  updating = c("batch", "incremental"),
  keep_history = FALSE,
  lapse_treatment = "no_lapses",
  noise_treatment = "no_noise",
  update_method = "label-certain",
  ...
)

## S7 method for classes <MVBeliefUpdatr::MNIX_IdealAdaptor>, <any>
update_template(
  x,
  observations,
  updating = c("batch", "incremental"),
  keep_history = FALSE,
  lapse_treatment = "no_lapses",
  noise_treatment = "no_noise",
  update_method = "label-certain",
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An NIW_IdealAdaptor, NIX_IdealAdaptor, or MNIX_IdealAdaptor object.

observations

A data.frame or tibble containing cue columns and, for update_method = "label-certain", a category column.

updating

Either "batch" or "incremental". Batch updates are currently supported only for update_method = "label-certain". Default is "batch".

keep_history

If TRUE with incremental updating, return a list of all intermediate models followed by the final model. Default is FALSE.

lapse_treatment

Treatment of attentional lapses during updating for label-uncertain models: "no_lapses", "sample", or "marginalize".

  • "no_lapses": Lapses are ignored; updating reflects pure normative evidence evaluation (even if lapse_rate > 0).

  • "sample": Simulates stochastic attentional lapses on individual observations. With probability lapse_rate, a lapse occurs and the observation is treated as uninformative during updating.

  • "marginalize": Evaluates updating in expectation across infinitely many encounters; evidence is downweighted by \(1 - \lambda\).

Default is "no_lapses".

noise_treatment

Treatment of perceptual noise during categorization for label-uncertain updating: "no_noise", "sample", or "marginalize".

  • "no_noise": No perceptual noise is applied to input cues, and no noise is assumed during categorization.

  • "sample": Simulates sensory noise on a specific observation. Noise drawn from \(\mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma_{\text{noise}})\) is added to input cues (and projected into composite cue space in early integration), and the observer accounts for their own noise uncertainty during categorization by adding \(\Sigma_{\text{noise}}\) to their likelihood scale.

  • "marginalize": Evaluates categorization in the limit across infinitely many noisy encounters (expected consequences). No noise is sampled onto the input stimulus, but \(\Sigma_{\text{noise}}\) is added to the category covariance scale.

Default is "no_noise".

update_method

One of "no-updating", "label-certain", "nolabel-criterion", "nolabel-sampling", "nolabel-proportional", or "nolabel-uniform". Default is "label-certain".

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

Value

An updated model, or a history of updated models when requested by a method.

The updated model, or a list of intermediate models when updating = "incremental" and keep_history = TRUE.

See also

update_category_representation

Examples

mod <- example_niw_ideal_adaptor(n_cues = 2)
obs <- tibble::tibble(
  category = factor(c("/b/", "/d/")),
  VOT = c(10, 15),
  f0_semitones = c(-1, -0.5)
)
updated <- update_template(mod, obs)
